summary: The stated remediations are present, but round 3 found two high-severity integrity gaps plus two medium defects. The runtime trusts routing metadata that is not proven to be compiler-derived, concern references can silently fail open, duplicate override values can violate the committed schema, and the reserved fallback prevents normal active-mode selection.

findings.claim: Runtime freshness verification does not prove that the routing index was generated from its canonical inputs, allowing routing metadata or required-skill membership to be altered without detection.
findings.analysis: verifyIndexFreshness compares canonical file hashes against hashes embedded inside the same untrusted index. An edited index can retain those embedded hashes while changing aliases, descriptions, invocation_policy, risk, or the skills array. Per-record SKILL.md hashing covers only records still present and does not prove routing metadata or catalog completeness. Removing a required skill record is especially dangerous: concern resolution then silently drops that pin through addPin's unknown-name return. The CLI validate path uses the same insufficient check, while loadIndex's artifactHash is calculated but never authenticated or compared.
evidence: loadIndex computes artifactHash from the index bytes, but no caller compares it with an independently stored expected digest.
verifyIndexFreshness compares source bytes only to index.compiled_from values supplied by the index itself.
The per-record loop verifies rec.path content_hash but does not verify aliases, policy, risk, descriptions, record count, or equality with compile(root).
resolvePins.addPin returns silently when byName lacks a skill, so deleting a concern-required record suppresses its pin.
scripts/skill-router.mjs validate calls verifyIndexFreshness rather than recompiling and byte-comparing the artifact.
findings.proposed_fix: At load or validation time, recompile canonical inputs in memory and byte-compare the result with the committed index, or authenticate the artifact with a digest stored outside the artifact. Fail to read-only diagnosis on mismatch. Add a negative test that changes policy metadata or removes a required skill while preserving compiled_from hashes.

findings.claim: The compiler does not validate concern-registry skill and rule references, so typos in critical governance bindings can compile successfully and fail open at runtime.
findings.analysis: concerns/REGISTRY.json is parsed only as a fingerprint input. Its handled_by.required_skills and handled_by.required_rules references are never checked against includedSkills or the known rule set. At runtime, unknown required skills are silently ignored, while unknown rule identifiers are emitted as if meaningful. This violates the compiler invariant that broken dependencies and unresolvable rule identifiers fail compilation and can erase a required security or governance skill from a confirmed concern match.
evidence: compile() executes JSON.parse(registryBytes.toString("utf8")) with the comment "fingerprint input only" and does not retain or validate the registry object.
Compiler reference validation is limited to overrides entries' requires and required_rules fields.
resolvePins.addPin contains `if (!byName.has(name)) return`, silently dropping unknown concern-required skills.
Concern required_rules are appended without checking them against knownRules.
The malformed-input validator covers duplicate manifest skill names but has no negative fixture for invalid concern references.
findings.proposed_fix: Parse and structurally validate every concern. Reject each handled_by.required_skills entry absent from includedSkills and each required_rules entry absent from the canonical rule registry. Add negative compiler fixtures for both cases and ensure the failure names the concern and invalid reference.

findings.claim: Override arrays can still make the compiler emit an index that violates its own JSON Schema.
findings.analysis: The F-016 type guards verify only that selected fields are arrays of strings. The schema additionally requires uniqueItems for aliases, requires, and required_rules. Duplicate aliases owned by the same skill pass aliasOwners because only cross-owner collisions fail, and requires/required_rules have no duplicate check. Since neither compile nor validate performs full schema validation, such output can be committed as nominally valid.
evidence: skill-routing-index.schema.json declares uniqueItems:true for aliases, requires, and required_rules.
The override guard checks Array.isArray and element types but not uniqueness.
The alias collision condition fails only when `owner && owner !== name`, allowing a repeated alias for the same skill.
requires and required_rules loops validate referenced identifiers but do not reject duplicates.
scripts/skill-router.mjs validate does not validate the artifact against skill-routing-index.schema.json.
findings.proposed_fix: Reject duplicates after normalized comparison for aliases and exact comparison for requires/required_rules, then validate generated output against the committed schema. Add one negative fixture for each uniqueItems field.

findings.claim: The reserved ambiguity fallback occupies cards[0], preventing normal active-mode candidates from ever reaching the auto-selection gates.
findings.analysis: The F-013 remediation reserves route-workflow by inserting it at the head before ranked candidates. Selection then runs only when cards[0] is not the ambiguity fallback. Therefore, whenever route-workflow is not already pinned—the normal active-routing case—the selection block is skipped regardless of the best ranked candidate's policy, confidence, margin, and risk. Current suggest-only policies conceal the defect, but the advertised active-mode surface will not work when Wave 4 enables implicit-allowed skills.
evidence: Active mode pushes a route-workflow item with reason_codes `["ambiguity-fallback"]` before iterating ranked candidates.
No later code evaluates the highest-ranked non-fallback card.
The existing active-mode corpus asserts only selected:null and fallback placement, so it cannot expose a valid implicit-allowed selection being suppressed.
findings.proposed_fix: Reserve fallback budget separately from ranked candidates. Evaluate the highest-ranked real candidate first; insert route-workflow at the head only when gates fail or no candidate exists. Add a fixture using a temporary implicit-allowed low-risk record that must select when confidence and margin pass.
